articles.title: Weekend - China warns of countermeasures as US Treasury widens tech investment curbs to biotech
articles.desc: The proposal adds to already tense US-China relations and keeps headline risk elevated for Chinese technology and biotech stocks, including US-listed ADRs and the Hang Seng Tech index. Biotech is the sector most directly exposed, since it is the newly targeted industry and has relied more heavily on
articles.content: The proposal adds to already tense US-China relations and keeps headline risk elevated for Chinese technology and biotech stocks, including US-listed ADRs and the Hang Seng Tech index. Biotech is the sector most directly exposed, since it is the newly targeted industry and has relied more heavily on cross-border funding than areas already under restriction. Beijing has not named the countermeasures it might take, and that vagueness tends to keep investors cautious until the response becomes clear. A long public comment period leaves time for negotiation, but it also stretches the uncertainty out for months, which could weigh on risk appetite toward China-exposed assets and the offshore yuan if rhetoric escalates. -- Washington wants to stop US capital from funding China’s next generation of strategic technology, and Beijing is signalling that it will not take the move quietly. Summary: On Thursday the US Treasury proposed a rule expanding the Outbound Investment Security Program, tightening limits on US investment in hypersonics, quantum, high-performance computing, supercomputing and AI in China, Russia and North Korea The rule also adds biotechnology to the targeted sectors, an addition sought by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent China’s commerce ministry said on Saturday the move discriminatorily widens China-related restrictions, overstretches national security and would damage bilateral economic ties Beijing said it will monitor developments and reserves the right to take unspecified countermeasures The proposal faces a public comment period before a final rule is issued Separately, the State Department this week sanctioned five Chinese companies linked to former Google engineer Linwei Ding, convicted this year of stealing AI trade secrets, drawing further objections from Beijing China has urged the United States to reconsider a proposed rule that would further restrict American investment in its technology sector, warning that the measure would harm trade relations and that Beijing reserves the right to retaliate. China’s commerce ministry voiced firm opposition on Saturday in a statement carried by the state-run Global Times, according to a report by The Hill. A ministry spokesperson said the proposal widens China-related investment restrictions in a discriminatory way and described it as a classic example of stretching the concept of national security too far. The ministry said it would watch subsequent developments closely, warned the rule would damage economic ties between the two countries, and said China retains the right to take corresponding measures, without specifying what those might be. The US Treasury Department unveiled the proposal on Thursday. It would expand existing restrictions under the Outbound Investment Security Program covering hypersonic systems, quantum information technologies, high-performance computing, supercomputing and artificial intelligence. The program aims to stop a small group of countries designated as foreign adversaries, namely China, Russia and North Korea, from using US capital to advance their own technological capabilities. The proposed rule would also bring the biotechnology industry within the program’s scope, an addition that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had pushed for, according to a department press release. Bessent said the changes would strengthen the program and prevent adversaries from using American investment to build critical technologies that threaten US national security. The measure must go through a public comment period before Treasury issues a final version, leaving room for revisions and for further diplomatic exchanges in the meantime. The proposal lands days after the State Department imposed sanctions on five Chinese companies connected to Linwei Ding, a former Google engineer convicted earlier this year of stealing trade secrets related to artificial intelligence. Beijing also objected to those penalties, saying they seriously harm the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese businesses. Taken together, the two moves underline Washington’s widening focus on technology and capital flows as a front in its rivalry with China. Beijing’s eventual response is now the key variable for investors and policymakers alike. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.title: MoT holds workshop on Qatar Intelligent Transport Systems Strategy & Action Plan 2027–2037
articles.desc: DOHAA workshop conducted by the Ministry of Transport (MoT) on the Qatar Intelligent Transport Systems Strategy & Action Plan 2027–2037 has concluded, in attendance of numerous rep...
articles.content: MoT holds workshop on Qatar Intelligent Transport Systems Strategy & Action Plan 2027–2037 - Read Qatar Tribune on the go for unrivalled news coverage MoT holds workshop on Qatar Intelligent Transport Systems Strategy & Action Plan 2027–2037 MoT holds workshop on Qatar Intelligent Transport Systems Strategy & Action Plan 2027–2037 A workshop conducted by the Ministry of Transport (MoT) on the Qatar Intelligent Transport Systems Strategy & Action Plan 2027–2037 has concluded, in attendance of numerous representatives from relevant entities and key stakeholders. The Qatar Intelligent Transport Systems Strategy & Action Plan 2027–2037 is a brand-new strategic project being developed by the MoT to deliver a safer, more efficient, and more sustainable transportation ecosystem. As part of MoT’s approach to engage all parties concerned, the workshop discussed the progress made to date, highlighted key outcomes achieved, and touched upon upcoming phases, priorities, and future directions. The strategy aims to establish a uniform national framework to steer relevant entities’ efforts toward developing a safer, more efficient, and sustainable transportation ecosystem through strengthening governance, enhancing network management, optimizing the use of data, supporting innovation, and building institutional capacity. Over the past few years, Qatar has invested in building an advanced transportation ecosystem, which now serves as a fundamental pillar for economic and social development and as this infrastructure matures, the priority has turned toward enhancing operational efficiency and asset sustainability, improving integration among various entities, and leveraging technology and data to both support decision-making and deliver the best possible services to users, said Eng Reem Mohamed Al Marafei, civil engineer with the Road Affairs Dept, MoT. In this context, she noted, the Qatar Intelligent Transport Systems Strategy & Action Plan 2027–2037, which is currently in the making, goes beyond the mere adoption of modern technologies as it focuses primarily on establishing an integrated framework for governance and institutional coordination, enhancing the effectiveness of decision-making, and improving the efficiency of implementation and monitoring—all in step with the goals of QNV 2030, thereby contributing to the realization of national objectives, and maximizing the value derived from future investments. The successful delivery of this strategy depends on effective inter-stakeholder partnerships, and shared commitment to developing an ITS that supports economic growth, enhances the quality of life, and strengthens Qatar’s regional and global profile, she noted. Eng Al Marafei said that developing the transportation ecosystem is no longer a single-entity responsibility; rather, it is a collective undertaking that requires stakeholders’ integrated roles and aligned efforts.

articles.title: 5 Google Messages Settings You Should Change Right Now
articles.desc: Now that Samsung has discontinued its Samsung Messages in the U.S. market, Google messages is the default texting app on Android smartphone.
articles.content: 5 Google Messages Settings You Should Change Right Now 5 Google Messages Settings You Should Change Right Now Whether you're fighting for more privacy or want to try new features, you'll want to dig deeper into Android's Google Messages app. A few hidden toggles can turn off RCS indicators, schedule your texts, or auto-delete verification codes to help conceal your activity. It's worth a closer look, especially since Google Messages is now the predominant texting app on Android phones; it used to compete with Samsung Messages. But times have changed: over the last year, the Korean giant has made Google Messages the default messaging app on its Samsung phones and officially retired Samsung Messages in U.S. markets in July 2026. As such, Google Messages isn't going anywhere; it's proven reliable (aside from a few technical hiccups) and a core part of the Android package. Still, that doesn't mean you should stick with the defaults or keep settings you set long ago, before other customizable features were added ; your main texting app should feel completely yours. Even if you are diligent about using verification codes sent through Google Messages quickly to log into your chosen services, it's still better to keep them off the record from unauthorized, prying eyes. This is because expired verification codes still leave a paper trail of which websites or apps you're using and confirm they are connected to your number. That's why the less information you keep on the front end of your messages, the better. Thankfully, this is easy to do. You can either do it manually or use the app's auto-delete setting. No matter which method you prefer, auto-deletion is still a solid option if you forget to clean up your messages (it doesn't hurt to enable it). To turn this setting on, open Google Messages, then navigate to "Messages settings" > "Message organization." From there, turn on "Auto-delete OTPs after 24 hours." When it comes to on-device AI features, there usually isn't a middle ground; you either like integrating Gemini into your apps or you don't. In the right hands, it can be useful, but otherwise it can feel like bloat. Nonetheless, the choice should remain yours, and if you don't want to see the Gemini button in your view, consider turning it off (it is currently the best option since Google didn't add Connected apps settings for Gemini in Google Messages). This keeps your messaging experience simpler and clearer. To get a more Gemini-free experience, open Google Messages and go to your "Messages settings." From there, go to "Gemini in Messages" and ensure the "Show Gemini button" toggle is set to off. Unfortunately, removing Gemini in this way doesn't improve your privacy, since it only hides the button from your view. If you're privacy-conscious, you can do a little more by turning off some Smart features embedded in the app. To do this, open Google Messages, tap "Messages settings" > "Suggestions & Actions." From there, select "Suggestions," "Suggested stickers," "Actions," and "Nudges" to turn any of these features off by tapping on the respective toggles. If you're a fan of gestures, Google Messages' swipe actions are quite easy to set up and manage inside the app. Essentially, they give you more control by letting you assign left and right swipe gestures to "Archive," "Trash," "Mark as read or unread," or "Off." To set them up, go to Google Messages, then go to "Messages settings," scroll down, and select "Swipe actions." From there, choose the "Swipe right" and "Swipe left" headers, then tap "Customize" next to each. This opens a pop-up window with a radio button next to each option. By default, the app assigns the same function to both, so you'll want to change it. Conversely, if gestures aren't for you and you accidentally move the conversation out of view, you can return to the same menu and choose the "Off" option to deactivate them. articles.desc: Things continue to get more exciting for Elon Musk's brainchild.
articles.content: Prediction: This Will Be SpaceX's Stock Price by the End of 2030 | The Motley Fool Space infrastructure and generative artificial intelligence (AI) are two of the hottest megatrends currently taking Wall Street by storm. And of $2.16 trillion, investors will naturally wonder if the company can still generate enough momentum to move the needle. Let's dig deeper into the pros and cons of SpaceX to decide what its stock might be worth by the end of 2030. Market cap calculated using publicly traded shares outstanding only. Does not include unlisted, private, or dual-class non-traded shares. Implied market cap may vary. Whenever a company goes public relatively late in its lifecycle, it makes sense to be suspicious about why. After all, no investor wants to be left holding the bag for a mature business that is done growing. However, SpaceX's recent results have totally dispelled these fears. Third-quarter earnings were a blowout with revenue surging 161% year over year, driven by momentum across all its segments. But the most interesting result was in AI, which management is now calling super intelligence (SI). This business involves acquiring data center computing power and renting it out to hyperscalers to run and train AI models, and it saw sales jump more than ninefold to $7.56 billion. There is reason to believe the momentum will continue in the coming quarters. Goldman Sachs expects hyperscalers' capital expenditure ( ) to reach $1.4 trillion next year, suggesting continued high demand for AI-related infrastructure. SpaceX's space infrastructure business is also doing well, with the company launching its first commercial Starship mission, which delivered 26 Starlink V3 satellites into low Earth orbit (LEO). What could a merger with Tesla mean for investors? But while SpaceX's earnings are impressive, that actually isn't the biggest news story for the company right now. SpaceX's future may be more influenced by a potential merger with Elon Musk's other public company, . Reuters reports that Wall Street now sees the combination as "inevitable." And both companies have formed special committees to discuss the idea, which Musk sees as "having a lot of merit." Off the bat, a merger makes a lot of sense. Both entities are headed by the same CEO (Elon Musk), and merging them will help avoid conflicts of interest. From an operational perspective, it will likely improve economies of scale and unlock cost savings by eliminating redundancies. This is particularly important as both companies are seeking to integrate generative AI and chip manufacturing into their business models. That said, the business combination could also come with challenges that make it harder to generate real value for shareholders. An alarming study by the accounting firm KPMG found that 83% of acquisitions failed to boost shareholder returns due to issues such as overpayment and poor synergies. A Tesla-and-SpaceX merger could have these issues in spades. of 352, Tesla stock is already extremely expensive. And SpaceX would likely have to pay a premium on top of that, leading to significant equity dilution, assuming this is an all-stock deal. Meanwhile, SpaceX investors will gain exposure to a stagnating EV business they may not want. Where will SpaceX stock be by the end of 2030? SpaceX continues to wow Wall Street with its explosive growth and successful transition to AI technology. And it remains one of the most exciting companies on the planet. articles.title: Netanyahu’s pitch: Can Israel use crypto to evade economic sanctions?
articles.desc: Prime Minister Netanyahu mulls cryptocurrency as answer to economic sanctions on Israel, but there are few buyers.
articles.content: Netanyahu’s pitch: Can Israel use crypto to evade economic sanctions? | Explainer News | Al Jazeera Two days before the general elections, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said that Israel should prepare to use cryptocurrency to circumvent potential sanctions on the country amid growing global isolation over its genocidal war on Gaza and settlement expansions in the occupied West Bank. Netanyahu on Friday said that blockchain-based cryptocurrency is the solution to bypass the mounting economic sanctions that would keep the country out of the international financial system. The Bank of Israel, the country’s central bank, rejected Netanyahu’s plan, and opposition parties said the incumbent prime minister’s vision is a recipe for disaster and increasing isolation. So, can Israel really circumvent sanctions by dealing in crypto? “We need to prepare ways to evade banking sanctions through an alternative economic system,” Netanyahu said in an interview with Israel’s Channel 10 last Friday. “You know what that means – the currencies that can bypass them,” he said, adding that he was referring to blockchain-based crypto. Netanyahu’s crypto pitch comes as Israel has been facing international isolation over its extreme policies against Palestinians: a surge in settler violence, anti-Palestinian rhetoric and the acceleration of illegal settlements in the occupied territories of the West Bank and East Jerusalem. Israel has killed more than 74,500 Palestinians since launching its genocidal war on Gaza three years ago. It has also been accused of committing war crimes in southern Lebanon, which has been hit almost daily by Israeli attacks despite a “ceasefire” now in place. Israel has also carried out attacks on regional countries, including Iran, as part of its expansionist , which is rooted in the biblical claim that Israel is entitled to the land between the Nile (in present-day Egypt) and the Euphrates (present-day Iraq). Netanyahu has vowed to expand settlements, which are considered illegal under international laws, and has reiterated that he would not allow the formation of a Palestinian state, drawing condemnation from his European allies. Last month, at least 12 major economies, including the United Kingdom, pledged coordinated measures against Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. The European Union has also sanctioned settlement-linked individuals and groups. Spain and the Republic of Ireland have introduced restrictions on settlement goods, while the Netherlands brought a broader ban on their import, purchase and sale into force in September. Israel’s banking system has not yet been targeted by sanctions. Moreover, Netanyahu also warned that Israel needs to look out for financing its own military, in the face of less support from Washington in bankrolling its wars – because “America has changed”. “It [financing] will end. It is only a matter of time,” Netanyahu said, adding that after US President Donald Trump’s tenure ends in two years, Israel should prepare for a less favorable White House. The United States funnels billions of dollars to the Israeli military annually, but the genocidal war on Gaza has changed unrestricted military support for Israel, which a growing number of Americans have started to question. Netanyahu also faces an arrest warrant by the International Criminal Court (ICC) for war crimes, while the International Court of Justice (ICJ) is hearing the case of genocide against Israel brought by South Africa. If the ICJ verdict goes against Israel, it would further intensify calls for sanctions against the country, including restrictions on arms exports, trade and financial ties, as governments around the world face mounting pressure to hold Israeli officials accountable. If Israeli banks are restricted from international transfers, then businesses could attempt to pay overseas suppliers using cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin, stablecoins, or other digital assets. articles.desc: Air India Express and IndiGo are shifting domestic and international flights from Mumbai to Navi Mumbai Airport, with a major focus on West Asia, transferring around 3 million passengers annually
articles.content: AI Express, IndiGo to move West Asia flights from Mumbai to Navi Mumbai - The HinduBusinessLine India-US interim trade deal remains stuck over tariffs, political concerns, sources Crude oil near $120, to intensify headwinds for economy, but tailwinds likely to reduce pressure Govt cuts wheat allocation in weekly auction even as millers ready to pay over ₹31/Kg IMD Update: Very severe cyclone threat for Bapatla-Vizag coast in Andhra Pradesh From 40% to fully Indian: WB Group VP on transfer of technology for Ukraine-Russia tested drones AI Express, IndiGo to move West Asia flights from Mumbai to Navi Mumbai The transition, which begins in December, will stretch into the next summer schedule https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/economy/logistics/ai-express-indigo-to-move-west-asia-flights-from-mumbaito-navimumbai/article71623866.ece The development is a major boost for Adani Group, which faces resistance from global airlines over shifting one-third of its flights from Mumbai to Navi Mumbai. | Photo Credit: ANI Air India Express and IndiGo are shifting domestic and international flights from Mumbai to Navi Mumbai Airport, with a major focus on West Asia, transferring around 3 million passengers annually. The transition, which begins in December, will stretch into the next summer schedule. The development is a major boost for Adani Group, which faces resistance from global airlines over shifting one-third of its flights from Mumbai to Navi Mumbai. It will also create necessary headroom for phased redevelopment of Mumbai airport’s Terminal 1, an executive said. In a joint statement on Sunday, Adani Group and IndiGo said 12 daily international departures will progressively shift from Mumbai to Navi Mumbai. This accounts for more than a third of IndiGo’s current international departures from Mumbai and includes destinations in West Asia such as Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, the UAE and Saudi Arabia. Additionally, flights to Dhaka and Jakarta, which depend on connecting traffic from West Asia, will also shift. “An additional daily service to Kathmandu will also be introduced, taking IndiGo’s international network at Navi Mumbai to 12 destinations between February and July 2027.” IndiGo will transition required domestic connectivity from Mumbai to Navi Mumbai to support these international flights. The capacity transition will create room for IndiGo to add new services from Mumbai to Asia, Africa and Europe besides developing another hub at Navi Mumbai airport. IndiGo holds slots for Central Asian destinations which it does not currently operate. Adding new foreign routes from Mumbai would not be a challenge. Air India Express will shift four domestic flights to Navi Mumbai in December. An existing flight to Muscat and a new service to Kuwait are planned from January. The Air India Group will progressively transition Air India Express services to Jeddah, Riyadh, Dammam, Doha, Muscat, and Sharjah, to Navi Mumbai with the process expected to be completed by the next summer season. The joint announcements suggest IndiGo and Air India’s flights to Dubai and Abu Dhabi will continue from Mumbai for now. IndiGo, which has a codeshare partnership with Qatar Airways, has also not announced a shift of its Doha services Mumbai Airport plans to begin redevelopment of Terminal 1 next January, which will require a partial closure of the facility. This would impact around 5 million passengers annually. According to the airport, the redevelopment necessitates the transfer of one-third of flights from Terminal 1 to Terminal 2 and from Terminal 2 to Navi Mumbai. Initially, the Adani Group proposed transferring flights in the winter schedule, which began today, but the plan was deferred due to airline objections. The Airlines Operators Committee has asked the airport to provide details of the Terminal 1 redevelopment plan, arguing that the facility handles less traffic than its design capacity of 15 million annual passengers. articles.content: It is often said that science and spirituality are locked in a permanent battle. This idea is known as the “conflict thesis” and it grew mainly out of Western history, where religious authority and scientific discovery clashed in some famous cases. The reality is far more nuanced than a simple war between two sides. Many scientists have been deeply spiritual and many spiritual traditions have encouraged careful questioning and direct observation. Dr Mrittunjoy Guha Majumdar’s book From Shiva to Schrödinger shows this very well from an Indian point of view. It does not treat science and spirituality as enemies and it does not try to make one defeat the other. Instead, it places Indian philosophy, especially Trika Shaivism, beside modern quantum physics and lets the two speak to each other. Ideas such as non-duality, interconnectedness and the role of the observer appear in both conversations, even though they are expressed in very different languages. The author explains these ideas in clear, simple words, so even a reader with no background in either field can follow. By the end, we see that Indian thought has long moved alongside the questions science asks about reality, mind and the universe. This makes the book a welcome and refreshing read for anyone tired of the old “science versus religion” argument. About Trika Shaivism The first chapters look at Trika, the philosophical basis of Kashmir Shaivism and set out its basic ideas in easy to understand language. The structure is based on three main principles: Shiva, which stands for pure consciousness; Shakti, the creative power behind existence; and Anu, the individual soul. It is these three principles that lead to the formation of the 36 tattvas, which stand for the various stages ranging from subtle awareness to the physical world. The text also mentions spanda, the original vibration that starts creation, and shaktipata, the descent of grace which brings about spiritual awakening. The author provides a historical context for these ideas by tracing the origins and development of the tradition and by pointing out the scholarly lines of succession, among others mentioning Vasugupta and Abhinavagupta, who have kept these teachings alive over the generations. The book also gives a important explanation regarding Trika’s view of the material universe. Unlike the traditional Vedic schools which consider the physical world to be illusory, Trika holds that the universe is a true and dynamic expression of Parama Shiva. The physical world is seen as the ultimate reality in terms of manifestation. This way of looking at things is put into practice using various systems such as the Yamala and Shakti tantras, Abhinavagupta’s three symbolic forms (vyakta, vyaktavyakta, and avyakta),\ and the Kaula practice, which focuses on three basic powers. Consciousness as the primary ground A central thesis of the book is that consciousness is not simply a byproduct of biological processes, but rather the foundational reality of existence. The text delineates three progressive levels of awareness para, para-apara, and apara, each representing a distinct degree of the same underlying consciousness. These are contrasted with the four experiential states: waking, dreaming, deep sleep and turiya. This perspective is connected to Para-vak, the primordial sound from which form arises and to the relationship between pramata (the knower) and prameya (the known). Trika conceptualizes awareness as an active force, characterized by the interconnected processes of knowing, willing and feeling. Rethinking the subject-object divide The book looks at the line that separates the observer from the external world and considers various approaches to this problem, mentioning John Searle’s analysis of subjective existence and objective knowledge, Mahayana Buddhism’s emphasis on emptiness, and Shankara’s Advaita philosophy of non-dual oneness. Trika’s particular method, known as pratyabhijna (recognition), does not aim at getting rid of the distinction between the self and the world, but rather seeks to bring about the understanding that this separation is in fact illusory; since all phenomena depend on a common fundamental field, pratyabhijna is able to resolve the apparent contradictions between unity and diversity as well as between the transcendental and the ordinary; the perception of a complete separation is finally seen as an illusion produced by the ego. Why classical physics shifted The text subsequently transitions to the historical development of modern physics. Newtonian mechanics provided effective explanations for macroscopic phenomena, such as planetary motion and everyday objects, but proved inadequate at the microscopic scale. In 1900, Max Planck introduced the concept that energy is emitted in discrete quanta rather than continuous waves. Building on Planck’s work, Heisenberg and Schrödinger formulated quantum mechanics, which underpins technologies such as transistors, lasers, and quantum computing. The book examines two foundational quantum principles: superposition, which posits that a system exists across multiple potential states until measured and uncertainty, which demonstrates that certain pairs of physical properties cannot be simultaneously determined(It is impossible to simultaneously measure both the exact position and the exact momentum of a subatomic particle). The author emphasizes that uncertainty is an intrinsic feature of nature, not a limitation of measurement instruments. The mechanics of entanglement The section dealing with entanglement is one of the most thoroughly discussed in the book. Once two particles are entangled, taking a measurement of one at once gives information about the other, no matter how far apart they are. This effect caused Einstein, Podolsky and Rosen to put forward the EPR paradox in 1935 and to claim that quantum mechanics was incomplete. Later on, Bell’s theorem offered a means of testing these ideas experimentally. The book then goes on to consider the main experimental loopholes locality and freedom of choice and demonstrates how modern experiments have systematically dealt with them. The text outlines how entanglement powers practical applications, including secure quantum communication, faster computation, precision measurement and advanced biological research. At the same time, the author clarifies a common misconception: while entangled states display strong correlations, they cannot be used to transmit actual information faster than the speed of light. articles.title: China's humanoid robots impressive on stage, unproven in factories: Report
articles.desc: China's humanoid robots impressive on stage, unproven in factories: Report
articles.content: China's humanoid robots impressive on stage, fail in factories: Report China's humanoid robots impressive on stage, unproven in factories: Report In 2026, a programme was launched to create over 100 high-value application scenarios and enable deployment of tens of thousands of units by end-2026, the report said. China's ambition to lead the next generation of technology through humanoid robots is facing a crucial reality check as impressive demonstrations struggle to translate into commercially sustainable mass deployment, according to a report. As per analysis of Capital FM Africa, from international trade fairs to factory showcases, machines capable of walking and manipulating objects have become symbols of Beijing's push into artificial intelligence (AI) and embodied intelligence, where AI interacts with the physical world. However, behind the spectacle, questions persist over whether the industry can move beyond choreographed routines to reliable, long-duration work in factories, warehouses and hospitals, it added. The Chinese government has identified humanoid robotics as a strategic emerging industry. In 2026, a programme was launched to create over 100 high-value application scenarios and enable deployment of tens of thousands of units by end-2026, the report said. The push comes even as regulators grow cautious, while Chinese regulators were slowing IPOs of humanoid robotics firms amid concerns that high valuations and state-backed revenues do not reflect underlying commercial demand. The core challenge remains economic viability, whether robots can operate safely in unpredictable environments and perform useful tasks at a cost that makes business sense. China does hold structural advantages, including extensive manufacturing capacity, dense supply chains and expertise in batteries, motors and sensors. "In March, China unveiled its first national standard system covering areas ranging from components and intelligent computing to applications, safety and ethics. More than 120 research institutions, companies and industry users were involved in developing the framework," according to Capital FM Africa. It further highlighted that a Shenzhen-based startup is reportedly using synthetic data and virtual simulations to train robots, reducing costs of physical-world training and has begun deployments in industrial settings. Yet government support itself raises questions of market discipline with early demand driven by funding and infrastructure before independent commercial willingness is proven. As robots become more connected and collect physical-world data, scrutiny over data security and technological dependence in overseas markets is also expected to rise, according to the report. "The crucial issue is therefore not whether China can build humanoid robots. It clearly can. The more important question is whether those robots can become sufficiently capable, reliable and affordable to generate genuine demand on a large scale," the report said. This report was published from a syndicated wire feed. Apart from the headline, the EdexLive Desk has not edited the copy. articles.title: Harbor Freight Just Dropped A New Color For Its Popular Daytona 3-Ton Floor Jack
articles.desc: Harbor Freight's Daytona 3-Ton Floor Jack is one of its most popular products with a near-perfect customer review rating. Now it comes in even more colors.
articles.content: Harbor Freight Just Dropped A New Color For Its Popular Daytona 3-Ton Floor Jack Harbor Freight Just Dropped A New Color For Its Popular Daytona 3-Ton Floor Jack When you walk into a typical garage or workshop, you may notice a frustrating, bland pattern of gray, black, and chrome. From hand tools like hammers to power tools that may offer only a small pop of color, your work space may be drab and uninspiring. Harbor Freight helps DIYers and craftsmen liven up their space with a variety of tools and storage options offered in bright colors like yellow and orange. These vibrant colors can also make it easier to spot a tool in a crowded garage. Daytona 3 Ton Low-Profile Superduty Floor Jack already available in multiple colors, including metallic green , metallic purple, and sunburst metallic orange. Now, buyers can also buy this popular floor jack in metallic racing blue. The new color is a nod to classic muscle cars and even features white racing stripes. This floor jack is exclusive to Harbor Freight. Currently priced at $289.99, the floor jack has an almost perfect 4.9 out of 5 star rating on Harbor Freight's website, a rarity in a time when most people only bother with a review when they're unhappy. If the heavy-duty floor jack is more than you need, Harbor Freight offers several other jacks in a similar, bright blue, though they lack the racing stripes. The Daytona 3 Ton floor jack is a good choice if you need a heavy-duty jack with rapid lifting, low-profile clearance, and a good price compared to competitors. The detailed specs on the Daytona 3 ton jack Whether you're doing a quick oil change or a full-scale restoration, the Daytona 3 Ton Low-Profile Superduty Floor Jack offers a professional-grade performance. Its low profile makes it a good choice for sports cars and other vehicles with low ground clearance. It has a minimum height of 3-¾ inches and a maximum height of 23-⅛ inches. The saddle pad is large, measuring 4-⅞ inches by 4-⅞ inches. It has what Harbor Freight has dubbed Rapid Pump, which uses dual parallel-pump technology to lift your vehicle with fewer strokes. The jack is made from all-welded steel and can lift up to 6,000 pounds (hence the "3-Ton" moniker). The hydraulic pump system has internal magnetic filtration to extend the life of the pump. The knurled handle grip helps you keep a solid hold, and a non-marring bumper helps protect your car's paint. When you're finished with your work, this jack has a universal joint release for smooth, controlled descent. Harbor Freight offers a three-year limited warranty on this product, which is available both in-store and online. Harbor Freight also sells the Daytona 3 Ton Long-Reach Low-Profile Professional Floor Jack with Rapid Pump technology and is available in a similar blue. It has a lower minimum height, higher maximum lift, and a longer frame reach, with similar outstanding reviews. Other items in the Daytona line (and sister Pittsburgh brand) include different types of floor jacks, dollies, jack stands , and more, with many products available in an array of bright colors.

articles.title: Tesla makes good on its Cybercab promise in just two weeks
articles.desc: Tesla Cybercab riders can now pull up a rear camera view and darken the screen. The post Tesla makes good on its Cybercab promise in just two weeks appeared first on TESLARATI.
articles.content: Tesla makes good on its Cybercab promise in just two weeks Tesla has given Cybercab passengers a way to see what is behind them, along with a way to turn the cabin screen off entirely. Riders in Austin can now bring up a live rearview camera feed on the Cybercab’s center display in the middle of a trip. Austin rider Ethan McKanna spotted the change late Friday night, posting from a ride that “You can now open the camera to view what’s behind you in Cybercab!” His photo shows a strip of rear camera video across the top of the screen, with another Cybercab following on a bridge. Sawyer Merritt shared the image Saturday and wrote that it “sounds like” there is also a new quiet mode that darkens the entire screen for riders who want to relax, sleep, or avoid a bright display at night. The camera view goes beyond the rear feed. Tesla UI software engineer Evan, who posts as @CarCoder, replied to McKanna with a tip: “You can also tap it to see more cameras, and swipe it up or down to hide and show.” Until now, the Cybercab only showed its rear and repeater feeds on the “Please Exit Safely” screen at the end of a ride, so passengers could check for cyclists and traffic before opening a door. Quiet mode surfaced a day earlier. Austin rider Jackson Blatz posted a video Friday morning of the new Robotaxi interface in a Cybercab with the option. Tesla has not published release notes for either feature. The rear camera view moved quickly from request to release. Earlier this month, Cybercab rider Dan Burkland asked Tesla to let passengers pull up the rear and repeater cameras whenever they want, “especially for peace of mind.” Evan answered “In development,” The feature fills a gap created by the Cybercab’s design. With no steering wheel, no pedals, no mirrors and no rear window, a passenger has no natural way to glance behind the car. The eight exterior cameras that feed Tesla’s autonomy software were already on board, so the change only required software. There is also an AI angle to how it was built. Yun-Ta Tsai, a senior staff engineer on Tesla’s AI team, quoted Merritt’s post and wrote that the “(human) camera view tuning is optimized with Grok and implements part of the algorithm by directly programming the fixed-function hardware, so I don’t even need to check the datasheet.” Tsai did not say which part of the algorithm Grok handled. Grok already plays a bigger role inside the vehicle, with Grok Bot and the Model Y Robotaxi fleet after Tesla The two features join a busy week of changes for riders in Austin, which also brought a redesigned Live Activity for iPhone and Apple Watch and live trip sharing. They also arrive as Tesla prepares the Cybercab for life outside its own fleet. On the third quarter earnings call, Lars Moravy said the company is aiming to deliver Cybercabs to customers before the end of 2026 . Tesla has not said whether the camera view and quiet mode will also come to its Model Y Robotaxis. Gene has been obsessed with cars since before he could legally sit in the front seat. Writer, researcher, unofficial CS support, accountant, native suit guy when needed, and overall stick poker. He approaches every story the way he approaches a road trip: with too much enthusiasm, not enough planning, and a surprisingly good outcome.
